## feature

<!-- new capability this task added -->

### homopolymer-smoothed deletion attribution

```
level: high
```

#### reason

The user's exact example ran end to end: two alignments of the same biological deletion produce `deletion=1` at positions 4 and 5 (the placement artifact) and `smoothed_deletion=2/3` at each of 4, 5, 6. 144 tests, ruff, and pyright pass.

#### description

```
type: [text]
```

1. `error.parquet` gains a 10th column `smoothed_deletion` (Float64, nullable): each deleted base spreads `1/run_len` over the maximal same-base reference run containing it.
2. `--fasta` (optional, faidx-indexed, same reference as the alignment) enables it; without it the column is null — "unknown", never confusable with "no homopolymer deletions".
3. Non-homopolymer deletions carry their full count at their own position; multi-base deletions smooth per base.

#### before

A deletion inside a homopolymer was attributed to the aligner-chosen position. Two alignments of the same read could split one event across two positions — demonstrated this session with `:3-a:5` vs `:4-a:4` over `TTTAAATTT`.

#### after

Per-position deletion profiles no longer carry the alignment-convention artifact; the plain `deletion` column remains for exact-event counting.

#### evidence

```
level: high
type: [text]
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}

- `src/sam_tagger/processing.py:105-118` — `homopolymer_run_span`.
- `src/sam_tagger/stats/error_stats.py:186-231` — `_smooth_deletion` (case-normalized cs-vs-fasta comparison, region clipping, one-time fasta-mismatch warning).
- `src/sam_tagger/stats/error_stats.py:333-344` — null-vs-0.0 normalization at write time.
- `src/sam_tagger/parquet_writer.py:150-225` — 10-column `PositionalErrorStats`, `smoothed_deletion` Float64.
- `src/sam_tagger/cli.py:176-183` — `--fasta` on `ErrorStatsArgs`; `src/sam_tagger/lib.py:407-414` — faidx wiring.
- Tests: `tests/test_processing.py` (run spans), `tests/test_stats.py:324-407` (5 smoothing tests), `tests/test_parquet_writer.py` (10-column), `tests/test_integration.py:484-503` (end-to-end with fasta).

:::

## limitation

### smoothing needs --fasta; genome-scale references fetch whole contigs

```
level: medium
```

#### reason

The cs tag's `:` ops carry lengths only, so runs are unknowable from the BAM (established this session); the whole-contig fetch is a code fact (`lib.py` `fetch(name)`).

#### description

```
type: [text]
```

1. Without `--fasta` the column is null — the feature is off, not approximated.
2. `get_ref_seq` fetches the full contig string per reference (cached per ref). Amplicon-scale references are trivial; a genome-scale BAM would materialize whole chromosomes.

#### evidence

```
level: high
type: [text]
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}

- `src/sam_tagger/lib.py` — `_get_ref_seq` calls `faidx_reader.fetch(name).upper()`.
- `src/sam_tagger/stats/error_stats.py:225-227` — per-ref sequence cache.

:::

## caveat

### mass identity holds only for runs fully inside the region

```
level: medium
```

#### reason

A test pins the clipped case: run crossing the region end drops the outside share, mirroring plain per-position deletion clipping.

#### description

```
type: [text]
```

1. `sum(smoothed_deletion) == sum(deletion)` per reference when every homopolymer run lies inside the error inner region.
2. Runs crossing the boundary lose their outside mass; do not assert the identity unconditionally on real data.
3. The uniform spread is the maximum-entropy convention, not a measured error model — the true position within a run is unidentifiable from a single read.

#### evidence

```
level: high
type: [text]
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}

- `tests/test_stats.py` — `test_smoothed_deletion_region_clipping`: region `[0,5)` keeps 1/3 at positions 4 and 5, drops position 6's share.
- `tests/test_stats.py` — `test_smoothed_deletion_user_example`: full-region identity asserted.

:::

level: medium

#### description

```
type: [text]
```

1. If a later analysis prefers edge-weighted placement priors, the per-base share in `_smooth_deletion` is the single point to change.

## conclusion

### the metric is delivered with the artifact demonstrated and removed

```
level: high
```

#### reason

The before/after comparison is measured on the user's own example, and the verification chain is green.

#### description

```
type: [statistic]
```

1. Same-event two-alignment demo: `deletion` splits 1+1 across positions 4/5; `smoothed_deletion` = 0.666667 at each of 4, 5, 6.
2. 144 tests pass (137 before; 7 new/extended), ruff and pyright clean.
3. Compute cost matches the assessment: one run walk per deleted base; deletion events are a small fraction of cs ops.

## process

<!-- audit of significant actions or decisions between plan and report -->

### three fixable defects found by the tests before shipping

```
status: wrong
```

#### description

```
type: [text]
```

1. Case mismatch: cs bases are lowercase (`-a`), the fasta is uppercased — the first run fell into the fasta-mismatch branch. Fixed by normalizing both sides.
2. Star-unpacking comprehensions in the 10-column writer were misaligned; replaced with index access, which cannot drift.
3. My own writer test passed the float last while the signature puts it 5th — the test was wrong, not the writer.
4. A wrong edit also dropped the `return pl.DataFrame(` line mid-refactor; the next run caught it.

#### evidence

```
level: high
type: [text]
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}

```text
assert 1.0 == 0.666… (case bug) → fixed
TypeError: 'float' object cannot be interpreted as an integer (unpacking) → indexed
TypeError: unexpected value … UInt64 (test arg order) → fixed test
```

:::

### null-vs-0.0 semantics decided during the run

```
status: right
```

#### description

```
type: [text]
```

1. The end-to-end test exposed that eventless positions read `null` with fasta present; the write path now normalizes to 0.0 when a reference was given, keeping `null` strictly meaning "smoothing unavailable".
2. A fasta referencing a missing file fails loudly (observed: `OSError: file … not found`) — no silent null fallback.

#### evidence

```
level: high
type: [text]
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}

- `src/sam_tagger/stats/error_stats.py:333-344` — the normalization.
- Session log: missing `hp.fa` raised OSError before the file was created.

:::
